en: In a vacuum, a feather and a bowling ball fall at the exact same speed because gravity accelerates all objects equally.
Magnets only attract specific ferromagnetic metals like iron, nickel, and cobalt, but do not attract aluminum, copper, or gold.
Static friction prevents a parked car from rolling down a hill even before the tires start moving.
Simple machines like pulleys do not reduce the total work needed, but they reduce the effort force required by increasing distance.
A lightbulb does not use up electrons, but only converts the electrical energy carried by them into light and heat.
Human eyes do not emit light, but we see objects because light from a source reflects off them and enters our pupils.
Sound travels much faster through solid steel than through air because the tightly packed particles in solids transmit vibrations more efficiently.
Coldness does not flow into objects, but a refrigerator cools food by physically removing heat energy from the inside and releasing it outside.
When a moving car brakes, its kinetic energy is not destroyed but transformed into thermal energy through friction between the brake pads.
If you break a bar magnet in half, each new piece instantly forms its own complete north and south magnetic pole.
A shadow is not a physical object but simply an area where an opaque object blocks light from reaching a surface.
Pushing a box up a gently sloping ramp requires less effort force than pushing it up a steep ramp, though the distance is longer.
